headline: Christian Ryan highlights valuation and liquidity as the two core risks investors must assess when allocating to private assets.
reasoning: Ryan acknowledges that getting into private assets is relatively straightforward given the number of options available, but notes that exiting can be difficult. He identifies valuation and liquidity as the two primary concerns most investors raise. He argues that independent valuation frameworks, governance, and compliance regimes adopted by many large managers can provide reasonable confidence in interim valuations, but emphasises that true value is only crystallised at the point of sale, making time-horizon alignment essential.
quote: Valuations and liquidity is probably the two core issues that most people ask and about. Many of the large organizations have independent organizations, and groups are a part of that. There's a whole, you know, compliance and governance and regime that exists amongst, uh, not all, but, you know, certainly many of these groups to determine, um, valuations. But I think a big component of that is one you're understanding what you're getting into. And secondly, the people you're dealing with, do they have all these controls and mechanisms in place. And at the end of the day, um, you know, value is obviously when, um, what people think it's worth buy or a sell.

headline: Private assets highlighted as a portfolio diversifier in volatile public markets, noting their illiquidity premium and absence of daily mark-to-market pricing
reasoning: Ryan argues that private assets provide valuable portfolio diversification in part because they are not priced daily, shielding investors from short-term volatility in public markets. He cautions that investors need patience and a long-term view given the illiquid nature of these assets. He analogises private assets to residential property — you cannot simply sell the next day — and emphasises the importance of picking the right assets and managers. Proper due diligence is identified as critical to navigating valuations in the private market space.
quote: The good thing about private assets, I believe, is that you're not, you know, in the main you're accepting, you're not pricing getting priced every day. And I think you've got to take a much more longer term view, but also you've got to be a lot more patient because at the end of the day, a lot of these assets, you can't just wake up tomorrow and sell it. You know, it's a bit like buying a home. You know, it's not like, you know, a home is a private asset. A property is a private asset. Um, it's not like you wake up tomorrow and say, I want to get my money and sell that that property. Sometimes it'll take three, six, 12 months. So if you've got patience and looking for some good diversification, you're just not going to get the volatility of daily capital.
